tier_reason: Tier C stands; usability moved from mixed to reference. The catalogued 0.5.4 numbers come from closed binaries, and the only public source (the v0.1.9 decoder) has a silent corruption bug: a u8 escape counter against a u16 count, so more than 256 escapes in a channel block corrupt the output with no checksum to catch it; it also has an unsigned underflow on PCM input under 24,576 bytes and a METADATA[16384] overflow. The FLAC and WavPack rows of the 0.5.4 table were copied unchanged from the 0.5.1 table (4 March) rather than re-run, and FLAC's MD5 verification work (none in HALAC) likely accounts for part of the decode gap. The 0.4.9 notes mention Rice coding, so the codec is not ANS-only.

corrections.caveats: Closed-source binaries produce the catalogued numbers; the public v0.1.9 decoder corrupts output silently past 256 escapes per channel block (u8 counter against a u16 count) and has an unsigned underflow on PCM under 24,576 bytes and a METADATA[16384] overflow. The 0.5.4 table's FLAC and WavPack rows are copied from the 0.5.1 table, not re-run; FLAC verifies MD5 while HALAC checks nothing. Not ANS-only (0.4.9 notes mention Rice coding).
